To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a simple normal mixture approach to gene expression analysis can be used to identify differentially expressed genes in a multiclass microarray experiment; (2) this approach is more accurate than other methods that we have tested; and (3) it is easy to use, requiring only a single parameter, the proportion of the population that is differentially expressed.

1. We have developed a simple and effective method for differential gene expression analysis of multiclass microarrays that can be applied to a wide variety of data types and that does not require the assumption that the data are normally distributed.
The normal mixture model is a useful and powerful tool for the analysis of differential gene expression in microarray experiments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing statistical models for the identification of differentially expressed genes in multiclass microarray experiments.
the following questions: (1) What are the most appropriate methods of analyzing microarrays? (2) How should we interpret microarray results?
the following question: how can one use the normal mixture model to identify differentially expressed genes in microarray experiments?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of the mixture model is a good idea for differential gene expression analysis, especially when the number of classes in the data set is large, and when there is no prior knowledge of the number of differentially expressed genes.
the mixture model approach to differential gene analysis is not a panacea for all microarray data.
, in the case of a normal mixture model, a simple implementation of a mixture approach to differential expression is not a good idea, because of the lack of robustness and the lack of power.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a simple implementation for the normal mixture model (NMM) approach to differential expression in multiclass experiments.
we have implemented a simple and fast algorithm to perform multiclass differential expression analysis on gene expression microarrays.
we provide an easy to use R implementation of the mixture model approach to differential expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have a new method for detecting differential expression in microarray data, which we call Mixture of T-distributions (MOT).
we have developed a novel method for identifying differentially expressed genes between multiple classes.
we have a very simple, yet powerful, way to analyze differential expression in multiclass experiments.
